key_insight: Dense user embeddings can be interpreted as sparse superpositions of meaningful behavioral modes.
engineering_relevance: Post-hoc mode extraction can make recommendation and personalization embeddings interpretable and queryable in natural language without modifying the upstream model.
method: Model user embeddings as sparse combinations of behavioral modes.
Recover modes with sparse dictionary learning, including sparse autoencoders.
Automatically name recovered modes and query them using natural language.
evidence_signal: Synthetic tests with known ground truth show better mode recovery by sparse autoencoders than classical sparse baselines, including for transformer-encoded embeddings; applications span two real-world datasets.
watch_item: The behavioral-mode interpretation is approximate for deep representations, so recovered modes and their natural-language labels require validation.
paper_title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
